<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4e0838d997d63a7662c839e6f1f914b22de475b2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

```sh

git fetch origin 33f3f01d0f2a99ce6ec05f42b7efe3ba881d2374 && git checkout 33f3f01d0f2a99ce6ec05f42b7efe3ba881d2374
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

Source context was read with `git show` only. Stamp: 2026-10-14T11:15Z.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`@objectstack/hono` `createHonoApp` catch-all: a repeated query name now reaches `dispatch()` as an array; it used to arrive as its last value.** This narrows. Every dispatcher arity rule becomes reachable on this host: the `/meta`, `/packages`, `/ui`, `/i18n` and `/security` refusals, and the `/data` filter slot. Each refuses `400` with its `RestServer` twin's code and sentence. **Right:** it is #6878's direction ("the handler must be able to SEE the ambiguity"). The construction mirrors `plugin-hono-server`'s module-private `readQuery`, as ruling A item 3 orders, and the docblock names the twin.
- **A single-valued name arrives as before.** It is pinned against the old construction's output. **Right.**
- **Genuinely multi-valued names (`select`, `expand`) now arrive as arrays.** That is what `RestServer` hands its own reads, and the round-1 census measured parity at the `/data` list. **Right.**
- **A `__proto__` name is now an own key, where the old dynamic write dropped it.** At a closed-set door it is refused as an unknown parameter; at the open `/data` list it is judged as a field (`INVALID_FIELD`). Both are loud. No prototype moves (pinned). **Right.**
- **An empty-name pair (`?=x`) is now dropped by Hono's parser, where the old construction delivered `""` and a closed-set door refused it.** One malformed input is newly admitted, and it matches the canonical `plugin-hono-server` adapter. It is declared in the changeset and graded `yes` by ruling `6166938503`, because no contract text could be cited for a `no`. **Right.**
- **`DELETE /packages/:id` refuses a repeated `keepData`, and `POST /packages` a repeated `overwrite`, on every host, with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` and `repeatedQueryParamMessage`, before any registry or protocol call.**
  - Before: `keepData` read a repeat as absent, so the protocol dropped object storage and answered `200` (`protocol.ts:25877`, `dropStorage = request.keepData !== true`). That was live on `plugin-hono-server` hosts. `overwrite` turned a `201` into a misnamed `409`.
  - The shape is the domain's own for `enabled` and `version`. The refusal pins assert `status`, `code`, the sentence and that the service was never called, beside preservation pins (`deletePackage` receives `{ packageId, keepData: true }` for one `true`). **Right.**
- **A one-element array is unwrapped in place** (the `status`/`type` rule). **Right.**
- **No exported declaration moves.** `readDispatchQuery` and `refuseRepeatedWriteFlag` are module-private. **Right.**
- **Excluded by ruling Q3 A:** P3 (`/analytics/meta ?cube`) and P4 (the share-link names) read a repeat as absent on this host, exactly as their canonical, already array-fed mounts do. No divergence opens. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- The changeset bumps `@objectstack/hono` and `@objectstack/runtime` `minor`, `fix(hono,runtime)!:`, BREAKING under the launch-window convention. **This matches** narrowed accept sets on two released packages, and `yes` takes at least `minor`.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` reads the same on the changeset's line and on the PR body's line 2. The marker is one ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; its prose names both the narrowing and the one widened malformed input. No `major`. **Consistent.**

  - A scratch probe was deleted and never staged. A lock queue-timeout is not cited as a measurement.
- **Out of scope:**
  - Slice 1's unreleased changeset ("until that adapter keeps repeats") stays byte for byte, by the precedent ruling B on #15953. This PR's changeset states the new reach.
  - #23265 (in flight) adds a `?expectedVersion` read point that refuses a repeat; it is consistent with this flip in either landing order.
